description: Content access control: identity-level DID-to-DID blocking (§3.6), per-member access key wrapping layer (§9.17, ADR-038), governance-gated content access actions (ADR-031), and unblocking with forward-only restoration. Three enforcement layers: key distribution denial (existing), SDK-mandated state destruction (new), access key wrapping (new). Three tiers: per-relationship in-context, identity-level cross-context, governance-gated per-context.

stories.title: Implement identity private state block list storage
stories.description:
Implement block list storage in identity private state per §3.7.1. Two granularities: global block list (Tier 2, cross-context) and per-context block list (Tier 1, single context). Block lists are append-only event logs with commutative operations (BlockDID/UnblockDID for global, BlockDIDInContext/UnblockDIDInContext for per-context). Current state is derived by replaying the event log.

Add ProtocolStore methods: get_global_block_list(), is_globally_blocked(), get_context_block_list(), is_blocked_in_context(). Implementations MAY maintain materialized views for query performance.

Multi-device sync is conflict-free because all operations are commutative — two devices can independently add blocks and the union is correct.

stories.title: Implement DID-to-DID blocking orchestration with cross-context propagation
stories.description:
Implement the blocking orchestration for Tiers 1 and 2 per §3.6. Tier 1 (in-context): block a DID in a single context — rotate sender key excluding the target (Layer 1, existing §9.16.3), trigger SDK-mandated destruction (Layer 2, §9.16.7), delete target's access key (Layer 3, §9.17). Tier 2 (global): block a DID across all shared contexts — store in identity private state (SCP-CAC-001), enumerate shared contexts, execute Tier 1 protocol in each.

Propagation is best-effort and idempotent — if the SDK is offline for some contexts, the block executes on next connection. The identity private state event log is authoritative; per-context enforcement is the mechanism.

Blocking is bidirectional: when Alice blocks Dave, both sides rotate their sender keys excluding each other (§9.16.3). The block notification is signed to prevent forgery.

stories.title: Implement DID-to-DID unblocking with forward-only restoration
stories.description:
Implement unblocking for Tiers 1 and 2 per §9.16.8. Unblocking reverses key distribution denial (Layer 1) but does NOT restore historical access. The blocker removes the target from their block list. The blocker does NOT rotate their sender key — the current key remains valid. On next SenderKeyRequest from the previously-blocked party, the blocker's SDK checks the updated block list and responds with the current sender key.

Historical gap is permanent: content encrypted during the block period used sender key epochs the blocked party never received and cannot retroactively obtain. Access keys destroyed during the block (Layer 3) are not restored for historical content.

Tier stacking: if governance (Tier 3) has also revoked access, the identity-level unblock does NOT restore access. Both must be independently reversed.

stories.title: Implement per-member access key lifecycle
stories.description:
Implement per-member access key generation, distribution, and storage per ADR-038 §2. Each context member holds an AES-256 access key generated at join time. Access keys are distributed via the pull-based protocol (same pattern as sender keys, §9.16.2): AccessKeyRequest/AccessKeyResponse wire types using HPKE with ephemeral X25519 keypairs.

AccessKey struct: 32-byte AES-256 key, context_id, member_did, epoch counter. Key material uses Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop for secure cleanup. Persisted to ProtocolStore under context/{context_id}/access_key/{did_hex}.

Access key generation is triggered by AddMember governance action execution. The executor generates the key and distributes it to the new member.

stories.title: Implement CEK wrapping and unwrapping in encryption pipeline
stories.description:
Implement CEK generation, AES-256-KW wrapping/unwrapping, and the WrappedContent wire format per ADR-038 §§2,4. Each message gets a fresh 32-byte CEK. Content is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the CEK. The CEK is wrapped with each recipient's access key using AES-256-KW (RFC 3394), producing a 40-byte wrapped key (32-byte CEK + 8-byte integrity check).

WrappedContent struct: ciphertext, nonce (12 bytes), wrapped_ceks (Vec<WrappedCek>). Integrity is verified by AES-256-GCM's authentication tag — no separate content hash field (storing SHA-256(plaintext) alongside ciphertext would create a plaintext confirmation oracle). wrapped_ceks uses truncated DID hashes (first 8 bytes of SHA-256(member_did)) as lookup keys to avoid publishing full DIDs. AES-256-GCM MUST bind context_id || sender_did || sequence_number as additional authenticated data (AAD) to prevent cross-context ciphertext relocation.

Layer ordering: access key wrapping occurs BEFORE sender key encryption (encrypted contexts) or broadcast key encryption (broadcast contexts).

stories.title: Implement SDK-mandated state destruction on block event
stories.description:
Implement Layer 2 (SDK-mandated state destruction) per §9.16.7. When a block event is received and verified, the blocked party's SDK MUST destroy all locally cached material from the blocking party: cached sender keys (all epochs), cached plaintext (decrypted message content), and cached access keys.

Destruction MUST occur before the SDK processes any subsequent messages — the block handler is synchronous with respect to message processing. This is a protocol requirement for compliant clients.

Also wire the complementary side: when the blocker's SDK processes a block it initiated, it deletes the target's access key from its local store (Layer 3 enforcement on the blocker's side).

Additionally, implement the ContentAccessState enum with four states: Full, ReadOnly, PresenceOnly, NonMember (§9.16.4). State transitions are one-way (block) until explicit RestoreReadAccess/RestoreWriteAccess governance actions. Forward-only restoration: unblock grants future access, historical gap is permanent. RevokeReadAccess triggers plaintext + access key destruction. RevokeWriteAccess triggers sender key exclusion (Layer 1). Both trigger the appropriate ContentAccessState transition.

stories.title: Add content access governance actions to GovernanceAction enum and wire execution
stories.description:
Add the five content access GovernanceAction variants to the enum per ADR-031: RevokeReadAccess { did, scope: RevocationScope }, RestoreReadAccess { did }, RevokeWriteAccess { did, scope: RevocationScope }, RestoreWriteAccess { did }, RotateContentKeys { reason: Option<String> }. Add RevocationScope enum with Full and FutureOnly variants.

Add corresponding GovernanceActionResult variants: ReadAccessRevoked, ReadAccessRestored, WriteAccessRevoked, WriteAccessRestored, ContentKeysRotated.

Wire execution in execute_governance_action() in ContextManager:
- RevokeReadAccess(Full): delete target's access key from all members, emit AccessKeyRevoked event
- RevokeReadAccess(FutureOnly): add target to exclusion list for future CEK wrapping
- RestoreReadAccess: generate new access key for target, distribute via pull protocol
- RevokeWriteAccess(Full): destroy target's sender/broadcast key, revoke messagesWrite UCAN, suppress historical content
- RevokeWriteAccess(FutureOnly): revoke messagesWrite UCAN only
- RestoreWriteAccess: re-grant messagesWrite UCAN, forward-only
- RotateContentKeys: rotate all access keys context-wide

This story depends on SCP-CAC-004/005 (access key layer) and on SCP-269 (GovernanceAction enum expansion) from the governance-integration PRD — the GovernanceAction enum and GovernanceActionResult enum must already include the content access variants before this story can wire their execution. SCP-269 is a cross-PRD dependency (governance-integration.json) and cannot be listed in blockedBy.

stories.title: Replace BlockAuthor with RevokeWriteAccess in broadcast context wiring
stories.description:
Update broadcast context author removal to use RevokeWriteAccess instead of BlockAuthor per §5.14.8. The existing block_broadcast_author() code path in ContextManager should route through RevokeWriteAccess { did, scope } governance action.

RevokeWriteAccess(Full) in broadcast mode: destroy author's broadcast key, revoke messagesWrite UCAN, deny key requests for that author, emit WriteAccessRevoked event. RevokeWriteAccess(FutureOnly): revoke messagesWrite UCAN only, existing broadcast key remains for historical decryption.

Remove any standalone block_broadcast_author() method or make it delegate to governance. Remove the AuthorBlocked event type — replace with WriteAccessRevoked { did, scope }.

RestoreWriteAccess in broadcast mode: re-grant messagesWrite UCAN, author generates new broadcast key (new epoch). Forward-only — previously suppressed content remains suppressed.
